newsitem.title: UK: UK holidaymakers dash to cash in before election.
newsitem.headline: UK holidaymakers dash to cash in before election.

text.p: British holidaymakers are dashing to cash in their pounds for foreign currency ahead of the national election on May 1, a travel company said on Monday.
Purchases of holiday money and travellers cheques are up 57 percent on the same period last year, according to British travel agent A.T. Mays.

"The only difference this year is the general election," said group managing director Malcolm Hewitt. "Shrewd holidaymakers believe the rates may take a tumble after May 1, and are advance buying their spending money."
A broad-based rally has seen the pound climb 93 percent against the Turkish lira, 21 percent against the Greek drachma and 24 percent against the peseta since April 1996.

A.T. Mays has seen a big increase in demand for Greek and Turkish currency -- usually a phenomenon of the July-September tourist season -- which has not been matched by a rise in bookings, a company spokesman said.
